en: Artificial general intelligence, or AGI, is
a term
you hear quite a lot these days.
And it's in the end a hypothetical category
of broadly capable AI with human-level or
greater general cognitive competence, which
simply means we're talking about AI models
that are so good
that they can perform kind of the same
tasks, at least on a computer,
as a human can,
often surpassing humans. Now, it's kind of a
difficult term because
at this point you likely won't find a model
that can do everything you can do
all the time the way you want it to do out
of the box. You need to steer those models.
They can get a lot of things wrong.
But these modern top models
definitely are extremely capable
and are therefore able to
really do already a lot of the things you
can do on a computer, and a lot of the
things they can do much better because
they're faster and, for example, because
they generate code on the fly to do some
calculations,
they are less prone to errors. So therefore,
it's up to you to judge if we already
reached AGI or not, if we do have models
that are truly better than humans.
It's fair to say that the top models are
better in many regards, but not necessarily
in all regards, I would say.
